risks.title: Dependence on general economic conditions
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned first in the ECONOMIC AND INDUSTRY RISKS section, with strong language on direct impact on customer demand, margins, and credit losses. It is repeated as a central factor affecting multiple aspects of the business. The Macro category is moderately weighted but the risk is central in the 10-K.

risks.title: Supply chain disruptions
risks.score_rationale: The text describes numerous disruption scenarios (natural, geopolitical, logistical) with direct impact on delivery capacity, costs, and profitability. The language is concerned and repetitive, indicating heightened vigilance. The Industrial category is moderately weighted but the risk is operationally critical.

risks.title: Cybersecurity threats and data breaches
risks.score_rationale: The risk is described in detail with alarming language on sophisticated cyberattacks, data losses, remediation costs, and reputational damage. It is clearly identified as potentially materially affecting results. The Cybersecurity category is highly weighted due to high digital exposure.

risks.title: Increased competition on pricing and market share
risks.score_rationale: The document emphasizes intense competition, particularly on pricing, with better-resourced competitors. The language indicates ongoing pressure on margins. The Competition category is moderately weighted but the risk is recurring and strategic.

risks.title: Volatility in procurement costs and prices
risks.score_rationale: The text stresses difficulty in passing through cost increases (products, energy, labor) and the negative effects of deflation. The risk is central to gross margin. The Capital category reflects the impact on cost structure and profitability.

risks.title: Dependence on authorizations from key suppliers
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly qualified as having a material effect on operations. Loss of a major supplier or changes in its distribution programs are described as potentially damaging. The language is concerned and the risk is strategic. The Industrial category is relevant as it relates to the value chain.

risks.title: Risks related to strategic acquisitions
risks.score_rationale: Acquisitions are described as essential to growth, but with high risks of integration issues, cost overruns, and failure to realize synergies. The language is cautious and repetitive. Although the Strategy category is not in the initial schema, it is implicit in Strategic and Operational Risks.

ai_positioning.summary: AIT does not mention artificial intelligence in its 10-K/20-F filing.
